content.user_title: Build Azure Document Analysis in Java
content.value_statement: Document analysis code can be slow to assemble from scattered SDK examples. This skill gives Java patterns for Azure Document Intelligence clients, prebuilt models, custom models, and classifiers.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure AI Form Recognizer Java package.
Demonstrates client creation with AzureKeyCredential and DefaultAzureCredential.
Lists prebuilt model IDs for layout, documents, receipts, invoices, cards, IDs, and W2 forms.
Provides Java patterns for extracting pages, lines, selection marks, tables, and fields.
Covers custom model build, analysis, composition, listing, deletion, and resource limit checks.
Includes document classifier build and classification examples for Java applications.
limitations: It is reference material and does not call Azure services by itself.
Users must provide their own Azure endpoint, credentials, documents, and storage locations.
Examples may need updates for newer SDK versions or service API changes.
It does not provide production security, retry, logging, or privacy policy design.

use_cases.title: Extract Invoice Fields
use_cases.description: Create Java code that sends invoices to a prebuilt model and reads returned document fields.

use_cases.title: Prototype Receipt OCR
use_cases.description: Use receipt examples to read merchant names, dates, line items, and confidence values.

use_cases.title: Manage Custom Models
use_cases.description: Build, compose, inspect, and manage custom document models from Java administration clients.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up the Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to add the Azure Document Intelligence Java dependency and create a DocumentAnalysisClient with environment-based credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Local PDF
prompt_templates.scenario: Extract layout information from a file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Java example that analyzes a local PDF with the prebuilt layout model and prints page lines and table cells.

prompt_templates.title: Process Business Documents
prompt_templates.scenario: Use prebuilt models for common documents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build Java logic that analyzes receipt and invoice URLs, validates field types, and handles missing fields clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Custom Model Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Java workflow to build a custom model from Azure Blob data, compose models, classify documents, and report resource limits.

output_examples.input: Request a Java receipt analysis workflow.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with client setup, model selection, field extraction steps, error handling notes, and credential placeholders.

output_examples.input: Ask how to read layout data from a PDF.
output_examples.output: A Java-oriented explanation that covers local file loading, polling for results, iterating pages, reading lines, and processing tables.

output_examples.input: Ask for custom model administration guidance.
output_examples.output: A workflow summary covering training data location, model build options, model composition, listing models, and checking service limits.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential for deployed applications when your Azure identity setup supports it.
Keep endpoints, keys, document URLs, and SAS URLs outside source control.
Check field types and confidence scores before using extracted values in business workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real Azure keys or customer document URLs into prompts.
Do not assume all prebuilt model fields exist for every document.
Do not delete or overwrite custom models without a separate confirmation step.

faq.question: What Azure service does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Document Intelligence, formerly called Form Recognizer, using the Java SDK.

faq.question: Can it analyze invoices and receipts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for prebuilt invoice and receipt models.

faq.question: Does it support local files?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to load a local document and analyze it with a prebuilt model.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It explains SDK usage after you already have an Azure resource, endpoint, and credentials.

faq.question: Can it help with custom document models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for building, composing, analyzing, listing, and deleting custom models.

faq.question: Is this skill useful in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Java SDK reference patterns that those coding assistants can use in developer workflows.
